subject.title: [Feature]: Merge iOS Privacy and Location card state

question: Should OpenClaw accept the linked iOS Settings UX direction that removes the standalone Location-derived Privacy summary and presents Location Sharing plus Access Level as the single Location state surface?
rationale: Source proves the duplicate state, but replacing the segmented picker with switch/value-row controls is a visible privacy UX decision and the open PR should not be treated as accepted solely because it implements the requested shape.

options.title: Review and land the linked narrow PR
options.body: Accept the single-owner Location card direction after PR review resolves any open implementation, i18n, and validation concerns.

options.title: Keep the current segmented model
options.body: Leave the issue open only if maintainers want Privacy summary plus segmented Location controls preserved for a broader future redesign.

options.title: Defer to broader location posture work
options.body: Use the broader Location Always/background-location issues for permission semantics and close or revise this issue only if the card-merge UX is intentionally out of scope.

recommendation.title: Review and land the linked narrow PR
recommendation.body: Accept the single-owner Location card direction after PR review resolves any open implementation, i18n, and validation concerns.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent iOS Privacy Settings work and co-authorship on Location Always changes make this the strongest routing signal for the UX direction decision.
